description:
FILED s473 (Fable, 2026-09-06) from the companion `--all --quick` on main + serial re-runs on main d348dcea AND on a `git archive 637fc58e` extraction (both 26/29, so PRE-EXISTING before BX; the fcf076f1 extraction says whether s470bw moved it -- see the s473 session-log).  The snapshot row `op/tiearray.t 75 0 40 35 DIFF` was STALE when the run compared against it.

THE ABORT (from `.suitelog/op_tiearray.t.fails.tsv`): `aborted-forms:1: Modification of non-creatable array value attempted, subscript -N PCL: tie: an ARRAY (class NegIndex ...)` at perl's t/op/tiearray.t line ~268, the STORE block of the NegIndex test:
    package NegIndex; $NegIndex::NEGATIVE_INDICES = 1;   # simulate indices -2 .. 2 (offset 2)
    tie my @n, 'NegIndex', ...; $n[-2] = 'a'; is($n[-2], 'a'); ...  # + DELETE/EXISTS over -2..2
PERL'S RULE (perltie, "NEGATIVE_INDICES"): for a tied array a negative index is normalised through FETCHSIZE UNLESS the tying class has a true package variable `$NEGATIVE_INDICES`, in which case FETCH/STORE/DELETE/EXISTS receive the negative index UNCHANGED.  `grep -i NEGATIVE_INDICES cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` finds NOTHING: PCL never reads the flag, so (a) the READ rows `is($n[-1], 'B')` normalise and fail, and (b) the STORE path reaches the #1273 fatal (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~4351 `Modification of non-creatable array value attempted`) which kills the enclosing form: the whole STORE + DELETE/EXISTS block, `n freed`, and the following NegFetchsize block are never produced (20 rows).

FIX SHAPE: ONE reading of the flag at the tied-array index normalisation (rule 11: the tie path of the aref/aset/delete/exists family shares a normaliser) -- `(p-package-var-true-p CLASS "NEGATIVE_INDICES")`, looked up once per tie (cache on the tie object), and the #1273 fatal stays for the UNTIED array (perl dies there too) and for a tied array WITHOUT the flag whose normalised index is still negative (perl: `Modification of non-creatable array value attempted, subscript -N` -- probe it).  Probe matrix vs perl 5.40.3: NegIndex FETCH/STORE/DELETE/EXISTS at -2..2; the same class without the flag; an untied array; `$#n`/`scalar(@n)` with NEGATIVE_INDICES; the NegFetchsize block (FETCHSIZE returning a negative size).  Guard rows in the tie guard file (find it); companion op/tiearray.t 26/29 -> toward 75/0 (say the number); the snapshot row spliced with this task as the cause.

WHERE IT BELONGS: a correctness filler (plan-post-s473 Â§2) -- the tie family; #155 (tie) is the umbrella.


=== MEASURED (s473h, Opus, 2026-09-08): THE FIX SHAPE ABOVE IS NOT AVAILABLE â BLOCKED BY #155 ===

The premise "PCL never reads the flag" is true but is not the cause, and the
fix shape presupposes a tied-array index normaliser THAT DOES NOT EXIST.

**`tie @array` is not implemented at all.**  `p-tie` refuses a raw aggregate
before any tie machinery is reached and says so on stderr
(cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `%p-warn-aggregate-tie`, the ruled non-support
`docs/not-supported.md` Â§"`tie` on an ARRAY or HASH  [INTERIM â¦]"):

    PCL: tie: an ARRAY (class NegIndex) is not implemented â the container
         is left untied (task #155)

So there is no FETCH, no STORE, no DELETE and no EXISTS to hand a negative
index to; `@n` is an ORDINARY array that never received the constructor's
elements, and every row in that block is measuring an untied array.

PROBE (scratch/s473h/probe/m9.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL at a9f2a264 â the class
and the NegIndex offset copied from t/op/tiearray.t; `t` prints the value or
the trapped die):

  spelling                perl              PCL
  $n[0]  / $n[2]          C / E             died (empty) / died
  $n[-1] / $n[-2]         B / A             died / died
  $n[-2] = 'a'            a                 dies "Modification of
                                              non-creatable array value
                                              attempted, subscript -2"
  $n[0]  = 'c'            c                 c        (the untied array)
  exists $n[-2]           1                 0
  delete $n[-2]           0                 0
  scalar(@n) / $#n        5 / 4             1 / 0    (the untied array)
  the SAME class WITHOUT the flag:
    $p[-1]                E                 died
    $p[-1] = 'z'          z                 dies, subscript -1
    $p[-9] = 'z'          dies, subscript -9   dies, subscript -9   AGREE
  an UNTIED array:
    $u[-9] = 'z'          dies, subscript -9   dies, subscript -9   AGREE
    $u[-1] = 'z'          z                 z                      AGREE

The three rows that AGREE are exactly the three that do not involve a tie â
which is the whole finding.  PCL's #1273 fatal is perl's own answer for the
untied array it is actually operating on; nothing about it is wrong.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE COMPANION NUMBERS: op/tiearray.t's 26/29 and the 20
missing rows are #155's cost, not a separate bug.  The file cannot move until
tied ARRAYS exist; the `$NEGATIVE_INDICES` rule is then one clause of that
implementation (the index normaliser the fix shape describes will be a real
place at that point), not a filler on top of it.

STATUS: kept OPEN as the record of perl's NEGATIVE_INDICES rule and its probe
matrix, but BLOCKED BY #155.  Do not schedule it as a filler again; a session
that picks it up will re-derive the same three minutes of measurement.
subject: REGRESSION (pre-existing at 637fc58e; found by the s473 companion run): a TIED array whose class sets $NEGATIVE_INDICES gets no negative-index pass-through -- the #1273 rule-12 fatal fires on `$n[-2] = 'a'` and ABORTS THE FORM, so t/op/tiearray.t reads 26/29 where the snapshot says 40/35 (20 rows never produced, 15 NEW fails)
